text: France is the dearest per kilometre (≈ €11 per 100 km for a car). 11 countries' motorways are free for a car — 5 of them with tolled bridges, tunnels or city charges (*) — and 8 sell a sticker for a period instead. [ 1 ] * Free motorways, with these tolls: Belgium — Liefkenshoek tunnel; Denmark — Great Belt bridge, Øresund bridge; Netherlands — Westerschelde tunnel; Sweden — Øresund bridge, Stockholm congestion tax, Gothenburg congestion tax, Sundsvall bridge, Motala bridge; United Kingdom — Dartford Crossing, M6 Toll, London Congestion Charge. Norway charges at automatic toll stations across the country. [ 2 ] Per-km countries show the typical rate we hold per country; exact rates differ by road (see the full data). Vignette countries show the shortest pass on sale. Spain €0 · Stockholm congestion tax €2.68 Driving Helsinki to Costa del Sol by motorhome (4,555 km, planned 11 Oct 2026), the Øresund and Great Belt bridges cost €225 together. Every French motorway toll on the same route came to €121, and Spain's toll-free autovías added nothing. [ 3 , 4 , 5 ] * secondary sources only; the operator publishes no figure we could read. Mont Blanc costs a car €56.40 one way; the Gotthard costs nothing beyond the Swiss vignette. The Brenner is €12.50 on top of Austria's vignette. [ 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 ] A 60-litre fill of petrol costs €65 more in Denmark than in Poland — more than the Brenner, Austria's 10-day vignette and the Great Belt bridge together (€57). [ 10 ] † Sweden: diesel currently costs well over petrol at the pump; national averages on 11 Oct 2026 were 18.83 kr (95) and 22.88 kr (diesel) per litre (bensinpriser.nu).
